## Tested scope and agreed goal

Reproduced on proposed [pm-vcs PR #126](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-vcs/pull/126), exact head `4de9d793074685ce5fb334eeff706fb0e484d709`. This concerns the unmerged feature, not a released-package incident.

The [annotation contract](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-vcs/blob/4de9d793074685ce5fb334eeff706fb0e484d709/ARCHITECTURE.md#L723-L744) promises last-native-setter attribution and the available origin changes of unresolved alternatives. The [canonical annotation feature](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-vcs/blob/4de9d793074685ce5fb334eeff706fb0e484d709/.agents/pm/features/pm-vcs-p7annotate.toon) requires correct change/author attribution and multiple origins for unresolved units.

## Reproduced defect

`Annotator.alternative` scans each parent file for the first occurrence of the alternative's text, then returns that occurrence's blame immediately. It does not establish that the matching occurrence corresponds to the disputed hunk. See [engine/annotate.ts lines 200–219](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-vcs/blob/4de9d793074685ce5fb334eeff706fb0e484d709/engine/annotate.ts#L200-L219).

Consequently an unrelated identical line in the first parent can supply the `theirs` alternative's origin, even though that parent never made the disputed edit. The result reports a confident but incorrect change ID and author instead of the actual available origin.

## Sanitized native-engine reproduction

A real temporary `Repository` was initialized. Each change used ordinary file writes, `stage` and `commit`; the branches were joined with production `merge(..., {recordConflicts: true})`. No store or merge mocks were used.

1. Author `initial` commits `text.txt` containing `theirs\nseparator\nbase\ntail\n`
2. Branch `other` from that commit; author `theirs-editor` changes only line 3 to `theirs`
3. On `main`, author `ours-editor` changes only line 3 to `ours`
4. Merge `other` into `main` with recorded conflicts
5. Call production `annotatePath(repo.objects, mergedHead, "text.txt", true)` and inspect the line-3 row's `alternatives` entry whose `side` is `theirs`

Expected: origin author `theirs-editor`, with the stable change ID of step 2.

Actual: origin author `initial`, with the stable change ID of step 1. The selected first-parent line is line 1, whose equal text is unrelated to the line-3 dispute.

Negative control: repeat the identical branch/edit/merge operations with initial line 1 changed from `theirs` to `header`. Attribution correctly names `theirs-editor`. The only change is whether an unrelated identical line exists.

The reproduction asserted the passing control and the incorrect repeated-text result. It used exact fetched production TypeScript under Node 24.19.0, disposable local repositories, fresh HOME, and disabled PM telemetry/agent probes. No live provider requests or original repository edits were required. Local SDK dependency was `@unbrained/pm-cli` 2026.10.18 rather than the source dev pin 2026.10.13; the demonstrated branch/merge/annotation path is native-engine code. This is an engine integration reproduction, not a packaged CLI or complete release-gate pass.

## Impact and regression acceptance

Conflict inspection can blame the wrong agent/change when common lines or snippets repeat elsewhere in a file. This is an attribution error; this reproduction did not demonstrate content mutation or loss.

- Add the real branch/merge scenario above and assert the exact disputed alternative's author and stable change ID
- Resolve an alternative's origin through hunk correspondence/lineage, rather than accepting any equal text elsewhere in a parent
- Cover repeated alternatives at different positions, multi-line alternatives, insertions/deletions shifting the hunk, and repeated occurrences with distinct authors
- Preserve the unique-text control and existing rename/copy, shallow-boundary and multi-origin behavior; do not replace a missing or ambiguous lineage with an arbitrary confident attribution

## Duplicate check

Checked all 126 current all-state issue/PR entries (two REST pages), current PR #126 discussion and review threads (no inline threads), and the canonical annotation/Phase 7 records. No matching defect was found. Closed #124 concerns overlapping text-conflict **resolution** splices and lost alternatives, whereas this issue is incorrect read-only annotation provenance.
Text-conflict annotation borrows an unrelated identical line's origin
